status.tpsEstimated: Estimated from stream chunks — the exact number arrives at the end of the step.

badge.partialWarn: Runs, but much slower (partially on CPU)
badge.hasProjector: This model also has a vision projector ({{size}}), downloaded separately when you want images.
badge.modelCtxMax: The model was trained for up to a {{n}}k window.
badge.estimateOnly: These numbers are an estimate: the file isn't here yet to measure. After downloading, the app measures for real.
badge.estimateCalibrated: Estimate adjusted by what we've already measured on this machine.

discover.title: Discover models

discover.empty: No models found. Try another search.
discover.gatedHint: Accept the license on the model page at Hugging Face and add your token in Settings.
discover.quantsHint: Fewer bits = smaller and faster file with slight quality loss. Green runs fully on your GPU.
discover.otherFormat: OpenWeights runs GGUF files with llama.cpp. MLX is Apple's format and doesn't run here; neither do safetensors, GPTQ or AWQ. The same model almost always exists as GGUF.

models.title: My Models
models.empty: No models downloaded yet. Go to Discover to grab your first one.
models.incompleteHint: Pick up where you left off, even after restarting the computer.

chat.title: Chat

chat.empty: Pick a model and start chatting.

hero.headline: How can I help?
hero.writePrompt: Write a clear, direct text about
hero.codePrompt: Help me write or review this code:

chat.noModels: You don't have any models yet. Download one in Discover.
chat.noServer: The AI engine starts automatically on your first message.
chat.loadingModel: Loading the model into memory (first time takes a while)...

effort.label: Effort
effort.hint: More effort means more complete answers, but takes longer and uses more memory.
effort.maxHint: No token cap. Can be slow and fill VRAM on large models.

chat.systemPromptPlaceholder: E.g.: You are a concise assistant.

ctx.label: Context window
ctx.hint: How much the model can remember in this load. Reasoning and the answer share this budget. More tokens use more VRAM.
ctx.notLoaded: The model is not in memory yet. Takes effect on the next load.
ctx.busy: Stop generation to reload the model.

engine.title: Model load
engine.hint: These apply at load time, not per message. Reload the model to take effect.

kv.label: KV cache
kv.hint: Conversation memory on the GPU. Compressing fits a larger window in the same VRAM, with a small quality trade-off.

flash.label: Flash attention
flash.hint: Faster generation at the same memory. Turn off only if the model fails to load.

spec.label: Speculation
spec.hint: Predicts tokens ahead. MTP uses layers already in the file; n-gram helps more on code.
spec.mtpHint: This file includes MTP — turning it on often speeds up generation.

vision.label: Vision
vision.hint: The projector uses VRAM. On demand loads it only when there is an image.
vision.none: This model has no vision projector.

kvOffload.label: KV on GPU
kvOffload.hint: On the GPU is faster. On the CPU frees VRAM and is slower.

engine.nglHint: How many layers go on the GPU. Empty = the engine decides.
engine.ncmoeHint: Expert layers kept in RAM. Helps a large MoE fit.
engine.parallelHint: Concurrent requests. More slots use more memory.

mmap.label: mmap
mmap.hint: Maps the file into memory. Turning it off copies the whole model into RAM.

mlock.label: mlock
mlock.hint: Locks the model in RAM so the OS cannot page it out. Only turn on if you have spare RAM.

voice.unsupported: Voice dictation is not supported in this environment.
voice.denied: Microphone permission denied. Allow access in Windows settings.
voice.network: Voice recognition failed. Check your connection.

chat.notSaved: Couldn't save this answer — it won't come back when you reopen the chat.

activity.title: Activity
activity.subtitle: What the agent has done on this machine, what it cost and what you approved.
activity.noPrice: A local model charges no money: the cost is your time and the tokens it spends.

calls.limit: Showing the {{limit}} most recent actions. Open a run to see the rest.

empty.title: The agent has not done anything on this machine yet.
empty.body: As soon as it reads a file, runs a command or touches your project, it all shows up here: every run with what it touched, the time and tokens it cost, and who approved each action — automations included, since those run with nobody watching.

server.title: Local Server
server.subtitle: OpenAI-compatible API so other apps can use your local models.
server.lanHint: Other devices on your network will be able to use the API.
server.needRuntime: Install the AI engine first (happens on first run).
server.modelsMaxHint: With 1, switching models unloads the previous one — what most GPUs can take. Above that, models stay loaded together and may not fit in video memory.
server.applyHint: The engine is running: stop and start it again for these settings to apply.
server.busyToApply: Can't restart the engine right now: {{who}} is using it. Finish or stop it, then apply again.
server.parallelHint: Each simultaneous conversation takes a slice of the context window. With 1, the window you ask for is the window you get.

connect.title: Connect
connect.noKeyWarning: any application with access to this machine can use the server.
connect.noKeyLanWarning: With network access on, any device on your network can too.
connect.testAuthStale: The key active on the server is a different one — restart to apply the new key.
connect.noModel: No model loaded — load one under Configure llama.cpp, right below.
connect.restartHint: The key change only takes effect after restarting the server.
connect.portHint: 1234 is LM Studio's port and 11434 is Ollama's — apps already configured for them connect without changing anything.
connect.anthropicHint: Claude Code and Anthropic SDKs point here — the client appends /v1/messages on its own.
connect.lanUrlsHint: For other devices, WSL or containers, use one of these addresses — 127.0.0.1 only works inside this machine. Windows Firewall may ask for permission on the first connection.
connect.lanUrlsOffHint: Apps in WSL or containers can't reach Windows' 127.0.0.1 — turn on local network access, right below, to use them.

stats.title: Serving stats
stats.avgHint: average over the range, not instantaneous
stats.serverDown: Historical numbers — the server is stopped.
stats.empty: Nothing served yet. Numbers show up as soon as any client uses the server — the chat here, the agent, or an external app.
stats.allClients: Counts all traffic the server handles: chat, agent and external apps (Claude Code, Cursor…).

cluster.title: Extra GPU on the network
cluster.subtitle: Another OpenWeights on this LAN can lend its GPU. Together they load a model that neither machine can hold alone.
cluster.security: The RPC channel has no password, and the pairing secret travels unencrypted on this network — good against a stranger who only knows the public name, not against someone capturing traffic. Only accept machines you recognise, never expose the port to the internet, and do not chat on this machine while lending the GPU.
cluster.noRpc: The installed engine does not include the RPC worker. Update the AI engine in Settings — both machines need the same llama.cpp version.
cluster.empty: No other OpenWeights visible on this network. Open the app on the other machine.
cluster.firstLoad: The first load sends weights to the other PC over the LAN — on gigabit, ~16 GB takes about two minutes.
cluster.enableHint: Off by default. Turning it on announces this app on the LAN and opens the control port — only on networks you trust.
cluster.off: Turn it on to see other OpenWeights on this network.
cluster.measured: The split was measured by the engine itself: it lists the real devices on both sides and how much each has free, instead of guessing from a percentage.
cluster.metalCap: macOS caps Metal at about 75% of unified memory, which is why this machine offers less than its total. Raising it takes a terminal and your password:

engineConfig.title: Configure llama.cpp
engineConfig.subtitle: Per-model configuration: recommended for your hardware, refinable flag by flag, applied on the next load.
engineConfig.noModels: No models in the library yet — grab one in Discover.
engineConfig.mtpMissing: This file's header doesn't declare an MTP head — if the model lacks one, the server will say so in the logs.
engineConfig.specNMaxHint: 3 is the default; 2–4 is the sweet spot. Beyond that it may destabilize and burn VRAM.
engineConfig.specPMinHint: 0.75 avoids wasted cycles on long context.
engineConfig.draftModelHint: A small model that drafts for the big one — on its own, enables classic speculation.
engineConfig.degraded: Couldn't read the binary's --help — showing curated flags only. Install/update the runtime to see them all.
engineConfig.searchPlaceholder: Search flags (e.g. mtp, rope, cache-reuse, jinja…)
engineConfig.noMatches: No flag by that name in this build.
engineConfig.managed: Managed by the app — configure it in the server or cluster card.
engineConfig.typedNote: Covered by the controls above — use them to change this value.
engineConfig.globalNote: Process flag — configure it in the "Global flags" card below.
engineConfig.needsRestart: Changes saved — they take effect on the next server restart.

enginePresets.title: Presets
enginePresets.applyHint: Apply this preset over the current configuration

globalFlags.title: Global server flags
globalFlags.hint: Apply to every model. Process flags become llama-server arguments; the rest goes into the INI's [*] section — and a model's own setting wins over the global one.

harness.title: Open in a harness
harness.subtitle: Hand the loaded model to an external coding agent pointed at the local API.
harness.needLoaded: Load a model to enable the Open button.

settings.title: Settings
settings.hfTokenHint: Doubles search limits and unlocks gated models. Create a free token at huggingface.co/settings/tokens.
settings.clusterLink: Extra GPU on the network — open Local Server

webSearch.title: Web search
webSearch.subtitle: Without a key, the agent searches via DuckDuckGo — free, lower quality, and prone to blocking. With a Brave or Tavily key, results get better.
webSearch.apiKeyPlaceholder: Paste your Brave or Tavily key (optional)
webSearch.applyHint: Changes apply immediately, no app restart needed. On automatic, the key picks the provider (tvly-… means Tavily; any other key, Brave).

onboarding.gpuSummary: You can run models up to ~{{size}} entirely on your GPU.
onboarding.cpuSummary: No dedicated GPU: small models will run on the CPU.

workspace.empty: No text files in this folder.

agent.unsupported: This model does not advertise tool support. Agent mode may work poorly.

mode.label: Authorization
mode.chatHint: The model only talks, it runs nothing.
mode.approveHint: Every tool asks for your confirmation.
mode.smartHint: Reading runs on its own; writes and commands ask first.
mode.yoloHint: Runs on its own inside the project folder. A checkpoint is created before the first change.

codeMode.label: Code Mode
codeMode.hint: The agent writes a program that uses the tools all at once instead of asking for one per step: fewer round trips, far less context. Requires Node on the machine.

yolo.confirmTitle: Enable automatic mode for this run?
yolo.confirmBody: The agent will create files, edit them and run commands inside the project folder without asking. Actions outside the folder, network access and commands we cannot parse still ask. A checkpoint is created before the first change.
yolo.needWorkspace: Pick a project folder to use automatic mode.

approval.title: The agent wants to use {{tool}}
approval.denyReason: Tell the agent what to do instead...
approval.opaqueWarning: We could not fully parse this command — review it before allowing.

terminal.title: Session terminal
terminal.empty: No command has run in this conversation yet.

run.maxSteps: Step limit reached ({{n}}). Ask it to continue if needed.
run.escalated: The agent got stuck on repeated errors and stopped for you to decide.
run.toolsRequested: The agent asked for more tools: {{tools}}
run.toolsUnsupported: No tools: this model's chat template can't take them.
run.toolsRejected: The server refused the request with tools — carried on without them.

checkpoint.confirmRestore: Restore files to this point? Later changes will be lost.

toolGroups.title: Tool families
toolGroups.subtitle: Turning a family off puts those tools out of the agent's reach.
toolGroups.windowHint: Even with every family on, the agent only gets the tools that fit the model's window — it asks for the rest when it needs them.
toolGroups.lastOne: Keep at least one family on. To stop the agent from using tools at all, pick "No tools" under authorization.

files.label: Files
files.desc: Read, create, edit and find files in the project folder.

code.label: Code
code.desc: Detect the project, build, run tests, lint and format.

git.label: Git
git.desc: See history and changes, stage files and commit.

data.label: Data
data.desc: Preview and query CSV files and SQLite databases.

web.label: Web
web.desc: Search, open pages and download files from the internet.

memory.label: Memory
memory.desc: Keep what should be remembered in later chats.

project.label: Project index
project.desc: Search the indexed project files by meaning.

plan.label: Planning
plan.desc: Split the task into steps and ask you when unsure.

mcp.label: Connectors
mcp.desc: Tools lent by the MCP connectors you turned on.

desktop.label: Computer
desktop.desc: Clipboard, system notifications and opening files or links.

mcp.title: Connectors (MCP)
mcp.subtitle: Connect MCP servers to give the agent new tools.
mcp.name: Name
mcp.changedBody: Server {{name}} changed its tools since you approved it. Review before using it again.
mcp.argsHint: Space separated; use quotes for values with spaces.
mcp.headersHint: One per line, as Name: value.
mcp.testFirst: Test the connection to read the tools.

automations.title: Automations
automations.subtitle: A request that runs on its own every so often, even when you are away.
automations.toggle: Turn the automation {{name}} on or off
automations.name: Name
automations.promptPlaceholder: e.g. list what changed in the project today and what is still open.
automations.modelDefault: Use the first one in the library
automations.paused: Off — does not run on its own
automations.deleteConfirm: Delete the automation {{name}}? This cannot be undone.
automations.unattendedHint: Nobody is watching when an automation runs: on "{{mode}}" it stops at the first confirmation request and waits for you.
automations.waitingBody: The automation asked for a confirmation and won't continue on its own. Open the run to answer.
automations.appHint: The automation clock runs inside the app: with it closed, nothing fires. At the scheduled time the AI engine starts on its own.

memory.title: Memory
memory.subtitle: What the agent remembers between chats in this project.
memory.factPlaceholder: E.g.: this project uses pnpm, not npm.

rag.title: Project index
rag.subtitle: Lets the agent search project files by meaning.
rag.needModel: Download an embedding model to index (try nomic-embed-text or bge-m3).
rag.vectorOff: Vector search unavailable — using text search only.
rag.empty: This project has not been indexed yet.
rag.confirmClear: Delete this project's index? You can rebuild it later.

question.title: The agent needs you
question.hint: Click an option to fill in the answer, or write your own — the run resumes the plan where it stopped.
question.failed: Could not answer — this question may have been answered in another window.

plan.title: Work plan
plan.subtitle: Big tasks become small deliveries that fit the model's window.
plan.windowHint: Model window: {{ctx}} tokens — deliveries up to {{perTask}}

mode.planHint: Investigates and proposes the plan. Changes nothing until you approve.
mode.agentHint: Plans in steps and executes each one with proof of completion.
mode.loopHint: Runs the whole plan, checking each delivery before moving on.

tune.title: Tune for this machine
tune.measuring: Measuring what fits on your GPU…
tune.applied: Done — the engine restarted with this configuration.
tune.rolledBack: It didn't load, so I went back to the previous configuration. {{error}}
tune.partial: Doesn't fit entirely on the GPU: part runs on the CPU, much slower.

reason.ctx: A {{ctx}}-token window per conversation, costing {{kv}} of KV cache.
reason.kvCompressed: Compressed KV cache: more window in the same memory, with a loss you won't notice in conversation.
reason.flashAttn: Flash attention on: same memory, faster generation.
reason.fitsGpu: Fits entirely on the GPU: {{used}} of {{total}}, leaving room for the system.
reason.partial: Doesn't fit entirely: {{host}} stay in system memory, and that part runs on the CPU.
reason.alternative: If you want more window: {{ctx}} tokens would take {{used}} on the GPU.

fact.mtpHint: This file ships multi-token prediction. It may speed up generation — we haven't measured it on this machine yet.
fact.visionHint: This model comes with a vision projector. Loading it only when there's an image isn't ready yet.

tune.benchHint: Measures real tokens per second. Takes a few minutes and needs the whole GPU: the engine goes down while it runs.
tune.benchSuspect: The GPU heated up during the run, so the comparison between configurations may be skewed. Worth repeating on a cold machine.

spec.title: Speculation
spec.hint: Predicts tokens ahead to go faster. How much it pays depends on the machine and the kind of text, so we measure instead of assuming. Restarts the engine between tests.
spec.inconclusive: The difference is too small to be worth changing the setup. Here, speculation makes no difference.

history.title: Performance history
history.benchWarning: Measuring takes the server down for a few minutes while the test runs.
history.benchFailed: The measurement failed — check the server logs.
history.usageNote: Real usage is not sliced per GPU: chat responses don't record which card they ran on.
history.empty: No measurements yet. “Measure now” runs a real test with this model's current configuration and records the result in this series.
history.gpuSeries: The series is per GPU and driver: switching cards or updating the driver starts a new series.

providers.title: Model sources
providers.subtitle: Where your conversations are answered: your own machine or an external provider.

openRouter.title: OpenRouter
openRouter.subtitle: Hundreds of models behind one key. The catalogue below is public; the key is only needed to chat.

nineRouter.title: 9router
nineRouter.subtitle: A local router with its own dashboard: it puts accounts from several providers behind one address. Installed in an isolated folder, without touching the rest of the system.
nineRouter.uninstallWarning: Deleting the data removes the accounts and providers configured inside 9router. This cannot be undone.
nineRouter.sizeWarning: Installing downloads portable Node.js and the 9router package (a few hundred MB on disk). With antivirus active on Windows it can take 2 to 10 minutes.
nineRouter.passwordHint: Use this password the first time you open the dashboard. It only applies on the first boot — after that, the password you set inside it wins.
nineRouter.panelHint: The dashboard opens in its own window: that is what lets its session stick. Embedded in this screen the login never completes.

gateway.title: Single entry point
gateway.subtitle: One address that forwards to the local engine and to 9router by prefix. Useful to point another tool at OpenWeights without memorising ports.
gateway.notTunnel: This is not a tunnel: nothing becomes reachable from the internet. Optional — chat works without it.
gateway.exposeLan: Accept connections from the local network
gateway.lanWarning: With this on, any device on your network reaches your models without a password. Only enable on a trusted network.
gateway.noRoutes: No provider running. Start the local server or 9router.

issues.managed: managed by the app — use its own control
issues.duplicateOfTyped: already covered by the "{{detail}}" control above

n-gpu-layers.label: GPU layers
n-gpu-layers.hint: How many model layers live on the GPU. Empty = llama.cpp splits on its own (--fit).

n-cpu-moe.label: Experts on CPU
n-cpu-moe.hint: For MoE models, keeps expert weights of the first N layers in RAM — makes a big model fit a small card.

split-mode.label: Multi-GPU split
split-mode.hint: How to split the model across GPUs: by layer is the default.

main-gpu.label: Main GPU
main-gpu.hint: Index of the card holding intermediate results and KV.

no-kv-offload.label: KV off the GPU
no-kv-offload.hint: Keeps the context cache in RAM instead of VRAM. Frees video memory at a speed cost.

no-mmap.label: No file mapping
no-mmap.hint: Copies the model instead of mapping it. Slower start; may reduce pageouts.

mlock.label: Lock in RAM
mlock.hint: Prevents the OS from swapping the model out. Needs enough RAM for the whole file.

fit.label: Automatic memory fit
fit.hint: llama.cpp adjusts window and layers to what fits. Turning it off without fixing ctx and ngl removes the safety net.

load-mode.label: Load mode
load-mode.hint: How the file enters memory: auto, mmap, mlock, mmap+mlock or DirectIO. Replaces the old --no-mmap/--mlock.

ctx-size.label: Context window
ctx-size.hint: Tokens the model sees per conversation. Bigger = more memory for the KV cache.

ubatch-size.label: Physical batch
ubatch-size.hint: Maximum tokens per physical GPU pass. Smaller saves compute VRAM.

keep.label: Kept tokens
keep.hint: How many prompt tokens survive when the context fills (-1 = all).

context-shift.label: Context shift
context-shift.hint: On endless generation, drops the beginning instead of stopping when full.

cache-reuse.label: Cache reuse
cache-reuse.hint: Minimum chunk reused from cache via KV shifting. 256 helps prompts sharing prefixes.

cache-type-k.label: K cache type
cache-type-k.hint: Key-cache quantization: q8_0 halves memory with minimal loss.

cache-type-v.label: V cache type
cache-type-v.hint: Value-cache quantization — requires flash attention on.

flash-attn.label: Flash attention
flash-attn.hint: Optimized attention: less VRAM and more speed on supported cards.

rope-scaling.label: RoPE scaling
rope-scaling.hint: Context-extension method beyond training: linear or YaRN.

rope-freq-base.label: RoPE frequency base
rope-freq-base.hint: Base frequency used by NTK-aware scaling. Default comes from the model.

rope-freq-scale.label: RoPE frequency scale
rope-freq-scale.hint: Expands context by a factor of 1/N.

yarn-orig-ctx.label: YaRN: original context
yarn-orig-ctx.hint: Model's original training window (0 = model's own).

spec-type.label: Speculation type
spec-type.hint: How to predict tokens ahead: draft-mtp uses the file's own MTP head; ngram-mod repeats text patterns; draft-simple uses a second model.

spec-draft-n-max.label: Draft: max tokens
spec-draft-n-max.hint: Tokens drafted per pass. 3 is the default; 2–4 is the sweet spot — beyond that rejection and VRAM eat the gain.

spec-draft-p-min.label: Draft: min probability
spec-draft-p-min.hint: Only accepts drafts above this confidence. 0.75 avoids wasted cycles on long context.

spec-draft-model.label: Draft model
spec-draft-model.hint: Path to a small GGUF that drafts for the big one (classic speculation).

spec-ngram-mod-n-max.label: N-gram: max
spec-ngram-mod-n-max.hint: Maximum n-gram tokens used for speculation.

spec-ngram-mod-n-min.label: N-gram: min
spec-ngram-mod-n-min.hint: Minimum n-gram tokens used for speculation.

no-mmproj-offload.label: Projector on CPU
no-mmproj-offload.hint: Keeps the vision projector off the GPU — saves about 1 GB of VRAM.

image-min-tokens.label: Image: min tokens
image-min-tokens.hint: Floor of tokens per image on vision models.

image-max-tokens.label: Image: max tokens
image-max-tokens.hint: Cap of tokens per image — lower is faster, less detail.

lora.label: LoRA adapter
lora.hint: Path to a LoRA adapter (commas for several).

lora-scaled.label: Scaled LoRA
lora-scaled.hint: Adapter with its own weight, as path:scale.

control-vector-scaled.label: Scaled control vector
control-vector-scaled.hint: Control vector with weight, as path:scale.

threads.label: Generation threads
threads.hint: CPU threads during generation. Empty = llama.cpp decides.

threads-batch.label: Batch threads
threads-batch.hint: Threads during prompt processing (default: same as generation).

numa.label: NUMA optimization
numa.hint: Strategies for machines with several memory nodes.

parallel.label: Simultaneous conversations
parallel.hint: Slots served at once — each takes a slice of the context window.

no-cont-batching.label: No continuous batching
no-cont-batching.hint: Turns off dynamic batching of concurrent requests.

timeout.label: Server timeout
timeout.hint: Read/write deadline for connections, in seconds.

ssl-key-file.label: SSL key
ssl-key-file.hint: PEM private key to serve HTTPS.

load-on-startup.label: Load on startup
load-on-startup.hint: This model comes up with the server, without waiting for the first request.

stop-timeout.label: Stop timeout
stop-timeout.hint: Grace seconds before force-stopping the model instance.

dedup-cache-models.label: Hide cache duplicates
dedup-cache-models.hint: Hides duplicated cached models from listings.

jinja.label: Jinja templates
jinja.hint: Uses the Jinja engine for the chat template (needed for tools on many models).

chat-template.label: Chat template
chat-template.hint: Name of a built-in template (chatml, llama3…) replacing the file's.

chat-template-file.label: Template file
chat-template-file.hint: Custom Jinja template from a file.

reasoning-format.label: Reasoning format
reasoning-format.hint: Where the model's thinking appears: separate (deepseek) or inline.

reasoning.label: Reasoning
reasoning.hint: Enables the model's thinking mode (auto detects from template).

reasoning-effort.label: Reasoning effort
reasoning-effort.hint: Level asked of the template: minimal to max.

reasoning-budget.label: Reasoning budget
reasoning-budget.hint: Token cap for thinking: -1 free, 0 off, N limits.

pooling.label: Embeddings pooling
pooling.hint: How to aggregate vectors on embedding models.

embeddings.label: Embedding mode
embeddings.hint: Restricts the model to the embeddings use case.

override-kv.label: Override metadata
override-kv.hint: Advanced: changes model metadata at load (KEY=TYPE:VALUE). Wrong values can corrupt the load.

override-tensor.label: Override tensors
override-tensor.hint: Advanced: forces the tensor buffer by name pattern.

no-op-offload.label: No op offload
no-op-offload.hint: Disables sending host tensor operations to the device.

check-tensors.label: Check tensors
check-tensors.hint: Validates model data at load (slower; useful for a suspicious file).
